analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: five changelog.d entries and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md. No Swift or Metal source and no threat-model YAML changed, so I found no concrete control regression. The changelogs describe source changes I could not see, so those behaviors are unverified.

Items for later passes, with relevant threat IDs:
- GLM video input (glm53-video-input.md:3): the provider decodes consumer-supplied inline data:video/mp4 and quicktime in-process. T-050 covers inline video plaintext in provider temporary files, A-001 covers the prompts. The changelog does not say whether the decode path writes temp files or uses an in-memory reader. This needs source review of the GLM video processor, and T-050 may need a GLM entry. Video and image rows also bypass the prefix cache, so they should not intersect T-041.
- Coordinator-served glm-5.3-flash (glm53-native-prerequisites.md:14): the changelog says the catalog entry, revision receipt and loaded bytes must agree on one aggregate. That bears on A-004 and T-012/T-027 (weight substitution), and the pre/post-load F_NOCACHE hashing (line 23) is the integrity control. Source review is needed to confirm the fail-closed checks and that the new capability glm5_next_v1 is not self-reported without hardware gating (TB-002).
- Prefix cache (T-041): the SSD store defaults on for GLM (line 9). A DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE path takes a persistent cache key from an operator file (line 21). The changelog says release builds do not contain it, so verify the #if DEBUG guard. New /metrics fields expose the cache failure detail and retained GLM faults.
- Local Responses continuation (local-responses-continuation.md, hardware-support.md:35-42): prompt, response and tool history now sit in two in-memory stores. The SDK object store has no matching eviction, so memory can grow without bound (A-001, local-mode availability).
- Retained-fault handling (lines 8, 16) is availability-relevant (T-016/T-029 class). The changelog says retirement without proof keeps resources and charges, so a persistent fault could strand GPU capacity until restart.

The unchanged-source claims in these docs are not verified here.
